records.reason: m178 at 20/1 fills the fixed-loading gap between 10/1 measurement 634f21e11a8442494ce3 and the severely underestimated 50/1 outcome 0c5c35afb3a24375c153. The current 17.21/50.46 mL prediction tests where both endpoints begin accelerating.

m199 at 2/1, 150 ul connects measured 1/1, 5/1, and 10/1 at the same loading and DCM plug. After accurate 5/1 but strongly underestimated 10/1 feedback, its predicted 11.13/19.79 mL endpoints locate the strong-solvent side of the sulfoxide transition.

m78 at 20/1, 100 ul anchors the curve below the delayed 50/1 measurement 61771d230b285babe4b6. Its 25.19/52.01 mL forecast tests whether the boundary failure reflects a localized transition. The existing 10/1 reference b5e6e9a4b5c6f0f838bd used 150 ul.

m94 at 5/1 starts a matched 5/1-to-10/1 pair between measured 1/1 54f20e9bd23ee1c7b5db and delayed 20/1 ffc70e28db22d1cc1f3f. This tests the onset of solvent sensitivity in the cyclopropyl beta-ketoester at unchanged loading.

m94 at 10/1 completes that fixed-loading pair. The predicted 30.63/58.90 mL endpoints discriminate gradual growth from a sharper transition into measured 20/1 retention, supplying more transferable information than another amount variant of the boundary label.

m80 at 20/1, 50 ul begins a controlled weak-solvent pair. Measured 10/1 ab66de7edad40236ffd5 was compact at 5.95/7.51 mL, whereas this forecast is 17.75/32.95 mL. The label tests a presently unmeasured transition in diethyl malonate.

m80 at 50/1 completes the matched pair, with predicted endpoints 30.52/65.44 mL. Together with the selected phenylmalonate boundary, it tests whether ester arrangement and substitution explain delayed elution beyond the compact measured strong-solvent region.

m75 at 50/1, 50 ul extends measured 5/1 c641cb5b9e82e60de614 at fixed conditions. Its comparatively compact 12.25/25.51 mL forecast contrasts with selected unsubstituted malonate m80 and delayed benzyl beta-ketoester m78, testing structural transfer rather than a common carbonyl correction.

m92 at 50/1, 50 ul preserves the EA loading protocol of measured 5/1 records 00f7bff5f3dab9ed9f49 and 790d27f0fa045d91f307. Its predicted completion of 14.69 mL is below those measured 21.06–24.40 mL values, testing an unusual decreasing alpha-ketoester response.

m82 at 5/1, 50 ul connects selected-round 10/1 measurement 3c041f5186a291c3b313 to its stronger-solvent region. With measured 20/1 ac81adfab5ec8ce768db, this creates a fixed-loading sequence that can distinguish acetoacetate curvature from the m94 and m80 responses.

m120 at 5/1, 150 ul directly contrasts amount with 50-ul measurement 71abc36775b6cce56da7 while preserving the DCM plug. The large onset-only amount contrast recently observed for m13 motivates testing whether such endpoint-dependent loading effects transfer to a methoxybenzyl alcohol.

m206 at 5/1, 50 ul supplies a fixed-loading continuation of 2/1 7c0c324643799c918828 and an amount contrast to 614873124b33029a924c. It separates the naphthylmethanol solvent transition from loading after completion remained underestimated at 10/1 in b7cf293311f83700cd9a.

m207 at 2/1, 50 ul fills the remaining strong-solvent gap in its matched 1/1, 5/1, and 10/1 curve. Measurements d803316212dc6eb862e9, 4e5ead91320bd24d485e, and a19f98569910dc7fd6c4 provide anchors for learning bromobenzyl-alcohol curvature without changing loading.

m208 at 10/1, 50 ul extends the sparse iodophenol coverage anchored by pure-EA observation 09b5473d1d8ee26da8d9. Paired nominal conditions with m209 test transfer between accessible phenolic donors bearing different substituents; density and plug differences remain covariates.

m209 at 10/1, 50 ul lies between measured 2/1 eda42a3c0f94ffce3e99 and 50/1 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf. It tests where completion growth begins for the trifluoromethoxy phenol and provides structural context for selected iodophenol, with the boundary loading difference retained.

m164 at 5/1 supplies the matched reference for its selected pure-EA measurement. The pair, plus measured 20/1 b7fffd840d208b29776c, tests the predicted completion minimum in a conjugated ketone without imposing a universal solvent-monotonicity rule.

m159 at 50/1, 100 ul probes a nitrile-substituted benzophenone after measured 5/1 b86ace0ccafe0af8ceec. Together with m114 and measured m178, it tests whether recent boundary failures generalize across aromatic molecules with two distinct acceptors; its DCM plug is retained explicitly.

Previously unobserved p-xylene m133 at 50/1 provides a compact-retention structural check against p-cymene measurement fec5b2d38184cff62e2c. Recent accurate compact labels make this a limited exploration choice, testing alkyl-substitution transfer rather than treating novelty itself as evidence of error.

m56 at 100/1, 50 ul tests the predicted benzoate plateau beyond measured 30/1 e19bda1298f299931245 at unchanged conditions. Accurate related isoamyl-benzoate outcome 8a288da5928f08936524 supports using this as a compact weak-solvent reference against the selected accelerating carbonyl families.

m181 at 20/1, 50 ul extends measured 10/1 2cc7c8ae52cdb25ca284 without changing loading. Comparing this fused lactone with measured fused-ring ketones tests how ring oxygen and ester functionality alter response beyond the established ring-size effect.

m182 at 20/1, 50 ul extends fluorenone measurement c9e08e156472783dee4e at fixed conditions. Its 12.55/37.47 mL forecast tests onset acceleration after the measured 10/1 onset remained 4.88 mL, adding a rigid carbonyl geometry to the ring-context comparison.

m118 at 20/1, 100 ul directly extends 10/1 observation 319e89d7000731f64e04, measured at 4.78/36.82 mL. The predicted 22.05/52.15 mL response tests whether onset catches up with completion in methoxybenzaldehyde, informed by the distinct thioether-aldehyde curve in d54c93a11164b4abac6e.

m59 at 50/1, 100 ul extends strong-solvent observation 19bdb9c6c59639662992 at fixed conditions. Its predicted 36.25/66.62 mL endpoints test whether methylenedioxy substitution transfers from aryl ketone f31a89256d8ee4192d55 to a flexible aldehyde whose carbonyl is separated from the ring.

hypotheses.content: Weak-solvent response compression is a local model failure across several acceptor environments. The m178 and m199 plateau forecasts failed decisively, but the correction should depend on acceptor identity, placement, and ratio rather than apply to all aromatic acceptors.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate labels identify the missing response curvature, while related compact forecasts test the limits of structural transfer and prevent a molecule-wide or acceptor-count correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m178 accelerate between 10/1 and 50/1, how early does the sulfoxide transition begin, and do methoxy- or nitrile-substituted benzophenones share either response?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl arrangement and substitution strongly condition solvent sensitivity. Benzyl beta-ketoester m78 and cyclopropyl beta-ketoester m94 entered delayed regimes, whereas benzoyl beta-ketoester m81 remained compact at 50/1. Malonates and the alpha-ketoester provide discriminating tests of transfer beyond this measured contrast.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched curves can teach structure-by-ratio interactions in a recurring ester family and constrain both endpoints after opposing historical errors among chemically related compounds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are m94 and m80 transitions gradual or localized, does phenyl substitution change the malonate boundary response, and is m92's predicted decreasing completion curve real?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing compounds have scaffold-specific solvent transitions. Recent m200, m120, m99, and m206 observations support substantial local growth, while m207's intermediate forecast was already close. OH accessibility and neighboring acceptors are plausible contributors; their mechanisms have not been measured.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local donor curves and linked phenolic exploration can improve chemical transfer without creating a universal alcohol or H-bond-donor offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How do the fixed-loading m206, m207, and m99 curves enter delayed regimes, and do accessible phenols and an ortho-hydroxy aldehyde change onset and completion differently?

hypotheses.content: Loading effects can differ by endpoint, scaffold, and ratio. At m13 10/1, raising sample volume from 50 to 150 ul advanced onset by about 16.08 mL while completion changed by only 0.93 mL. The m72 contrasts were smaller, and m195's unusual 150-ul 20/1 onset does not yet establish a smooth loading relationship.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A few targeted contrasts can teach conditional amount effects and endpoint asymmetry without spending the batch on largely redundant loading variants.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m13 onset-sensitive loading pattern transfer to m120 at 5/1, and does controlling m141 loading change the inferred solvent-response curve?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen environment and ratio jointly determine response. The methyl-anthranilate curve remained compact across new 5/1 and 20/1 labels, whereas ethyl anthranilate and m141 showed substantial weak-solvent growth. Earlier m211 overpredictions continue to contradict a nitrogen-wide upward correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These comparisons distinguish local curve errors from functional-class offsets and extend learning to a secondary amine with a controlled strong-solvent anchor.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does ethyl-anthranilate completion begin growing, what is m141's 5/1 response at the loading of its delayed labels, and does dibenzylamine become compact at 1/1?

hypotheses.content: Some predicted strong-solvent reversals may be extrapolation artifacts, especially in sparse acceptor environments. The previous m13 pure-EA-versus-2/1 forecast was reversed by measurement. However, cinnamic acid has a measured nonmonotonic completion response, so monotonicity cannot be imposed universally.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Strong-solvent labels can correct unsupported response shapes while preserving genuine exceptions arising from chemistry or unrecorded experimental factors.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is m164 completion actually later in pure EA than at 5/1, and does the sparsely observed phosphorus-containing molecule enter a compact 1/1 regime before its measured delayed 10/1 response?

hypotheses.content: Ring context affects aryl-ketone response beyond a constant offset. The m179/m180 difference persisted at 50/1, and their completion difference increased relative to 20/1. Extending this finding to fluorenone rigidity or a ring oxygen remains an untested structural hypothesis.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related fused-ring labels can teach carbonyl geometry and functional-environment interactions while distinguishing onset changes from completion growth.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed loading, do fluorenone and the fused lactone accelerate between 10/1 and 20/1 in ways that transfer from the measured cyclic ketones?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes reject the specific m178 and sulfoxide plateau forecasts: m178 at 50/1 was underestimated by 37.17/72.03 mL and m199 at 10/1 by 28.34/64.19 mL, while the matched sulfoxide 5/1 label was close. I therefore prioritize intermediate response points and structural controls for transfer. Large underestimates for m78 and m94 strengthen the structure-dependent carbonyl hypothesis; the compact m81 boundaries prevent interpreting this as a universal carbonyl effect. Ethyl anthranilate and m141 also grew well beyond their plateau forecasts, but new methyl-anthranilate measurements supported compact retention, reinforcing nitrogen-environment specificity. Alcohol feedback again varied: m120 and m99 were substantially underestimated, m206 completion remained underestimated, and m207 at 5/1 was comparatively close. The new low-loading m200 1/1 label was 15.15/37.40 mL versus 33.88/74.44 mL at 2/1 under the same protocol, supporting a solvent transition rather than an exceptional low-loading regime. m13's pure-EA label corrected the forecast reversal, and its 10/1 amount contrast revealed a large onset change with nearly unchanged completion. This justifies selective endpoint-specific loading checks. For m72 at 20/1, the new controlled DCM amount contrast was moderate; comparing the two 50-ul protocols still combines loading-solvent and plug-volume changes. The m195 50/100-ul 20/1 onsets near 10–12 mL and nearly identical 100/150-ul 10/1 onsets do not explain the old unusual 150-ul 20/1 record, so I do not spend another large block on that anomaly. The ring-size difference persisted at 50/1. Accurate compact m77, m147, and m55 outcomes, and earlier-than-forecast m188/m192 boundaries, temper novelty and high-volume acquisition. All stated forecast errors are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The 32 experiments combine failure repair with tests of where those repairs should generalize. Fixed-loading m94 and m80 pairs, the m178 intermediate, and the sulfoxide anchor locate missing solvent-response transitions. Carbonyl exploration compares beta-ketoesters, malonates, an alpha-ketoester, and substituted benzophenones, creating informative contrasts in functional-group arrangement rather than relying on polarity totals. Donor and nitrogen selections connect existing measurements into interpretable curves, while a small number of loading contrasts address the newly observed endpoint asymmetry. The m164 pair tests a forecast reversal directly, and the phosphorus pair constrains a sparse structural environment using its existing 10/1 label. Fused-ring and aldehyde experiments examine transfer to different carbonyl geometries and substitution contexts. P-xylene and the benzoate boundary provide linked compact-retention coverage so retraining is not driven only by delayed labels. Each selected molecule-plus-condition tuple is distinct, and no pending experiments exist. This batch should help the retrained predictor learn conditional curvature and separate V1/V2 responses across the Row-distribution; predicted interval width is not treated as uncertainty, and quantile widths are not used as calibrated epistemic evidence.
